folder_html:
Legend

Diffuse attenuation coefficient for PAR (m^-1), FIXED absolute scale LOWEST 0.016 clearest (dark blue) → 0.5 → 1.0 turbid (red) → 1.5 → HIGHEST+ 2 most turbid (deep purple), plus an isolated grey No-data swatch for cloud gaps. Larger values always mean murkier water; source values are never altered.

Diffuse attenuation coefficient for photosynthetically available radiation (KdPAR): how quickly sunlight fades with depth. Larger values mean more turbid water; smaller values mean clearer water. Source values are never altered for color convenience.

Exact variable: kd_par (Diffuse Attenuation Coefficient for PAR; NOAA MECB algorithm; product status Experimental)
Units: m^-1
Source: NOAA CoastWatch S-NPP VIIRS Kd(PAR) diffuse attenuation, Global 4 km, Daily (ERDDAP; newest-wins across nesdisVHNkdparDaily NRT and nesdisVHNSQkdparDaily Science Quality, per-day fallback)
Update: daily composites
Why turbid water turns red/purple: Fixed absolute scale with anchors where lake water lives: open-lake water spreads blue through yellow, coastal plumes read orange-red, and only rare very-turbid water (storm resuspension, river plumes, intense blooms) reaches violet/deep-purple.
Provenance: ERDDAP dataset
